a:r.a:t: Coenzymes are not a permanent part of the enzymes’ structure.
They associate, fulfill a function, and dissociate.
The function of CoA is to accept and carry acetyl groups.

p:cNvPr.descr: An image illustrating the coenzyme A (CoA) chain. The acetyl-CoA chain is at the bottom left, where C (blue) binds left to CH3 (blue), double binds up and to the right to O (blue), and binds down and to the right to S-CoA (where S is in red). Above that is the reactive thiol group, which has a wavy arrow point to the HS in the beta-mercaptoethylamine chain. this chain beings with a red HS and binds right to CH2, which binds right to CH2, which binds right to N. N binds up to H, and right to C (in red box), which begins the pantothenic acid chain. C double binds down to O and binds right to CH2, which binds right to CH2, which, binds right to N. N binds up to H and right to C, where C double binds down to O and binds right to C. C binds up to H, down to OH, and right to C.
